claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from cheaters, scripters, and connection manipulation like lag switches and DDOS attacks.

citations.review_text: To be so honest if you are new to this game it's really not worth it. Don't get me wrong I play frequently, but the amount of cheaters and scripters inn this game just take the fun out of it. And the ban recognition and response id absolutely horrid. Most instances i know of have someone getting banned 4 match after being reported, and in some cases they don't receive a perma-ban either. There are quite a few of players who I see often who are known cheaters and still continue to muddy the game of its fun. it's hit or miss with matchmaking as well. Sometimes you feel like you're a god at the game dropping 30 kills in a dominion just to get clapped the next game after by a bunch of REP 200+ players.

If you plan on playing For Honor in 2026 let me break it down for you, grab some popcorn for this one.

Cheaters: This game like any other online PVP title is filled with cheaters, how do you cheat in this game you may ask. Well there's scripters, DDOS attacks, lag switches, and much more that I cant name off the top of my head. Sounds like fun right? well we are just getting started.

Community: I have a total of 1,913 hours on this game from both console and PC, this is one of my most played games on my accounts and I can say with certainty that this is the most toxic, unemployed, cesspit of a community I've ever had to play with. Most seasoned veterans on this game like myself all share the same opinion and yet we still come back too it, why? ill answer that below.

The Games Origins: The game when it released 9 years ago was a huge hit in the industry, nobody had ever made a medieval style fighting game like For Honor which created a small but faithful fanbase for the game gaining about 10,000 players on average for the first year of release. Then 2018 came and the game saw a huge spike in players, the largest its ever had when over 250,000 people joined in August. When September came around the player count had dropped severely to only about 40,000 active players, then it was 20,000 in October, I'm sure you get the idea by now but the game could never retain a large player base. After that single spike the player count has remained at a stagnant 5,000 player average since June 2019, but where did everyone go and why within a 2 month timeframe? 

The Base Game: Your first time playing this game feels great, its a breath of fresh air in the fighting genre. Your first few matches go as expected which is multiple deaths and very few eliminations. You think to yourself, this game has quite the learning curve and you attempt to improve your skills. You learn how to parry heavy's and lights, guard breaks to near perfection, deflecting attacks, dodge timing, bashes, co…

im not gonna be a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but ubisoft fix the engine please

Boot up is a little clunky for Me, but it boots up and runs well after it does its thing.
In case it isnt clear, this is a button combo fighting game and each character plays differently.
I think the combat system is very fun, i like all the character designs and mobility. I also still enjoy playing against the AI and you can still level up against the bots, so im not forced to play insane pvp matches.
 I would like to see different game types and more expansion on the main story in general, but I have fun memories with friends while playing this game.
 Be prepared to lose all the time.  Enjoy the game for what it is, accept the challenge or uninstall it.
Trolls are everywhere, everyone loses eventually, and weather you continue to bash your head against a wall is your choice.  own it.

Can't speak for console players, but most of the negative reviews are due to people getting trolled or spam killed.  Unfortunately, thats just being online with other people.  Little to do with the game itself.  Dead by Daylight is much worse. 
 I put a lot of time in on console and a small chunk of time on pc.  I wouldve put more time into it if they would make the game size less than 115GB.
  The other main thing to remember is that if You look at Steam Charts, the same 4000=6000 people are still playing this game since 2018 and they're the ones you're playing against online. There is not much new players in general, so the game is probably going to match you up against someone who has been playing since release.  You won't win against someone like that.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a steep learning curve and requires practice to master combos and mechanics.

citations.review_text:
one of the most unique fighting games i've played, been playing on an off since 2018-19 from PlayStation, to Xbox and now pc in 2026. the game has gotten better over the years, but Ubisoft being Ubisoft is self explanatory.

the game is more fun now i will admit (with the sole exception of Juren, he should not have every unique in the game, unblock-able's / undodgables, hyper-armour, fast grabs, shoves, etc, you get the idea, although Ubi are doing good at listening to the community, they have nerfed him alot and he is now fun to play against ill admit) 

in 2026 this game is still hell, the same bugs from years still exist (you parry an attack, it goes through the animation and you die, it is more rare now ill say), community has 0 honor and is toxic a fair amount (it has gotten less toxic over the years) but they have improved alot, and coming back after 2 years of playing the new characters are pretty fun and fairly balanced

this is 100% one of those games u HAVE to get used to playing, and need to put in sometime to truly learn the game to have fun.

my summary: wait till a sale to buy or a free week to try it, it usually goes from 25 down to between 5-2 (the winter sale it went to 1.24) it is very fun to play and mess around in, even with friends, i recommend trying the game at least once but it will take more than 2 hours to get used to the game so refunds might not be an option, you WILL have to learn things for u people with cooked attention spans.

P.S. Ubisoft please update campaign

There's a steep learning curve, but when you get used to it, it because an intense highs peed action, and real time strategy to be able to control the points, and it does take a lot of practice to learn the combos, and actually utilize them when you're being attacked.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans praise the deep and satisfying combat system, but highlight a toxic community, steep learning curves, unhelpful tutorials, prolonged unlock grinds, and post-match crashes.

claims.claim: The game features a steep learning curve requiring significant time and patience for new players to understand its mechanics.

citations.review_text:
I primarily played on Xbox when playing For Honor for the majority of my game time (1700 hours give er take), ever since they recently added cross progression, I have completely switched over and now exclusively play on PC. With that in mind, For Honor is a game I would recommend getting on sale. I absolutely fell in love with the game back in 2017 during Year 1 season 5, however it was a buggy mess, frames were stuck at 30 and the servers were hot garbage.

I essentially grew up playing the game and thus saw the many ups and downs in its live service. Learning the game is relatively simple but has a deep combat system than what it presents itself. It is a constant game of chess, between your Hero's' interaction against the opponents. With the amount of Heroes in the game, it will take at least about 100 hours to get a grasp of everything. It may be daunting at first but it is worthwhile. Definitely the hardest part of getting into For Honor is your first 50 reps. You are going to get your ♥♥♥♥ rocked A LOT!

You will experience the whole spectrum of emotions (Mostly anger and hate) fighting either the enemy or quite frankly your rando teammates. I have essentially become a monk overtime to be able to ground myself so i don't go ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I have lost four controllers over the course of my career (not proud of that ngl). You will get tested a lot with your patience, a cool and collected mind will persevere greatly.

I'd say after 1200 hours I got decent at the game reaching Master Rank in duels, I never played competitive For Honor but that's a whole thing on its own. Part of your journey will be doing homework on the game, watching videos, studying frame data and keeping up with the patch notes for each season. The gameplay is unique and partly because Goobysoft patented the "Art of Battle System" which makes it quite literally like nothing else. 

The fashion when you reach the higher reps is lovely and what I mostly play for now of days, there is bountiful color pa…

Honestly, it's a dead game. No new permanent game modes have been added since the games release. MAYBE 1-2 maps, nothing impressive and both maps were ones the game already had, they just expanded on (copy and pasting the existing map into a new game mode and pretend like it's a whole big original idea?). The playerbase is subpar. "Skill based" matchmaking is a joke. They keep adding new heroes hoping it'll revive the game but its player count gets lower and lower every year. Constant bugs. No casual games, just you trying to enjoy the game only to fight 4 stack after 4 stack after 4 stack and if you quit because it's such a dogwater experience, you'd BETTER believe you're going to be penalized 15 minutes before you can play another game. There's ZERO balance. There's ZERO fun. It's an impossible learning curve, and I say this as somebody that's been playing the game for like 6 years. It USED to be an amazing game. Now it's a dumpster fire. Full of toxic losers that just run around in groups DESTROYING literally EVERYBODY, both new players and vets alike simply by ganking 3-4 v 1  with overpowered heroes. Devs refuse to acknowledge this. Community keeps abusing this. Your average player continues to get more and more fed up. Campaign in this game has produced nothing but memes. This whole game has become a laughingstock of what it means to play a something that's nothing but ragebait. 
I've already uninstalled for the last time. Do yourself a favor and don't even give this steaming pile of feces a chance. It's not worth your time. It's not worth your money. It's not worth the frustration.

It's a dead game trying desperately to cling to any sort of life it can find. Typical parasite behavior.

Steep Learning curve , requires patience and devotion to learn and master , but rewarding. requires decent , but not high end hardware. DLSS is bugged with a memory leak , but FSR seems to work fine. Great tool for training your anger management , haha! Console+PC combined hours 2,5k.

For Honor is one of the few games that ive played since the first few months, i was there for the mess that was original centurion and ive attempted to be there for every hero release since.

The game has many ups:
1. a one of a kind combat system thats relativley easy to understand
2. interesting heros with unique mechanics for eqach of them
3. some great cosmetic options
4. a dev team that interacts with community figureheads 
5. some much needed changes for heros over the years

but with its ups it also has its downsides:
1. heros that remain unbalanced for extended periods of time (eggregious examples are new release heros)
2. a new player unfriendly tutorial that forgets to explain some very important key features
3. friendly fire that will interrupt your own combos
4. people with anger issues that rivals other games such as siege
5. "scripters" (people who use external software to read the screen and react to attacks acordingly)

I mostly want to stress, this is not a casual friendly game. if you treat it as such you will be miserable the entire time. there will be things you will have to learn outside the tutorial and if youre not willing to do that you will severly hinder youself and others. but take the time to learn the intricacies of the game and you will have a lot of fun :)

ALSO VERY IMPORTANT:
honor is not treated as an obligation, what you think is cool and friendly will backfire on you when the guy youre giving a 1v1 to gets his friends to come stomp on you. be "honorable" at your discression.

Steep learning curve and it's not for everyone, you have to think when playing this game.
Predictions are a very big thing which is why some people will argue it's not skill based, but actually it's exactly what makes this game good, it requires some brain activity and a fast reaction time. Whether or not your opponent will feint their attack is unknown but you can make reads based on your opponents play style which makes the game very enjoyable. 

To new players, don't spam side dodge attacks.
You WILL get parried.

This game is also rage inducing to the point of wanting to destroy your setup so please stay calm.

game is like a toxic relationship w ur ex , you'll love it one day but the next you'll be disgusted. if ur slightly depressed this game is perfect for all the pent up anger, both through the game or your moniter's face card. would rate it 10/10 very unique and in all honesty if you truly take the time to learn the game it becomes a lot more enjoyable. you will not be anywhere close to mastering the game at 100 hours, but i do recommend trying the game out. the community is pretty good most days especially at low reputation which is like your level in the game. idk try it out don't be discouraged from your start it's like learning to fight in real life you gunna get your ass handed to ya for sure, but worth the patience to get good.

[h1] My Honest Review [/h1]

[h3] PROS: [/h3]
- Flashy animations, edgy characters and immersive combat is there.
- Character identities are well put. Voice lines and their playstyle are unique.
- Keybinding customization support both for PC and Console is available.
- Local pricing is available on Ubisoft Store for ingame items.
- Lots of customization options for characters
- Lots of room for strategies, team play and micro/macro gameplay with different objectives/win conditions
- The combat feedback feels so good. The flashing guard UI before a hit, the deflect animation with lots of sparks (particle effects) and guardbreaks are all visually satisfying and noticable which makes combat feel smooth.
- Teamplay makes the game so much more fun and easy. If you have premades, macro and teamfights are easier compared to randoms.

[h3] CONS: [/h3]
- Learning curve is steep because it is almost like a fighting game. A lot to remember and execute.
- Bot systems are horribly designed. A bot will immediately leave and be replaced with a new connecting player in the middle of combat, revive, or capturing an objective. VERY ANNOYING and UNPREDICTABLE.
- Ubisoft sells heroes in a game about heroes vs heroes. And by pure chance, as luck would have it, new heroes are slightly better/stronger. So you have to pay to buy them or do daily missions for 10-14 days to unlock ONE.
- As long as you have a teammate, something will MOST LIKELY will go wrong, even if you're a really high reputation or ranked player. For example: Someone will interrupt your unique character grab attack (Sohei, Shaman, etc.) and relentlessly fill enemy's Revenge bar so that both you and him can die.
- Game doesn't teach you much, tutorials are outdated. Story Mode abilities and characters abilities and mechanics are irrelevant to current state of the same character in multiplayer mode. (Which is also why nobody really understands how Revenge system works)
- You have to level up each character seperately by le…

What I can't get over, however, is that every single new character for the past couple of years was just "throw every single game mechanic into it, plus more".

Maybe, it's just failure to adapt and a skill issue, but I stopped having fun playing this game.

Get it on a sale, the game is like $2 during those, and well worth it. Just not fun to me anymore (which, yeah, I played it for a fair bit.)

For Honor stands as a strong title that is only limited by a handful of smaller issues and technical hiccups Ubisoft should address. Its story campaign falls short of the best in the genre, and the matchmaking system still needs refinement. Even so, none of that changes the core truth: the game offers some of the deepest and most satisfying combat mechanics to appear in years. For Honor requires real dedication to learn its systems and master them, but players who invest that time will discover an experience that has few equals in gaming today.

I played thousands of hours of League in my time, known for being the most toxic community, but the players in this game are exceptional, and far more petty.

The balance is non-existent, and there is no end to weird technical issues. I'm on a 4090 with 30 ping and I'm constantly lagging, and at less than 5fps.

There are no fun matchups, they are all insufferable, unless the hero was released within the first year of the game's release, but anyone playing those heroes have sunk thousands of hours into the game and destroy you like an ant caught at the center of a thermonuclear explosion.

It also just feels like the rules of the game and it's mechanics never work the way you expect; you're punished for everything, and rewarded for nothing.
